newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's IFIL 1996 net profits rise six pct.
newsitem.headline: Italy's IFIL 1996 net profits rise six pct.

text.p: TURIN, Italy (April 15) - Italy's financial holding group IFIL said on Tuesday that its parent company 1996 net profits rose six percent to 138 billion lire from 130 billion in 1995.

The group added that it was considering the purchase of a stake in Italy's largest banking group San Paolo di Torino in part of the bank's privatisation programme, but IFIL was awaiting conditions for the purchase.
IFIL and IFI are two holding companies controlled by the Agnelli family which together control the Agnelli's stake in automotive and industrial group Fiat which amounts to around 32 percent.
IFIL hold stakes in Italian retailer Rinascente and also French industrial companies including consumer group Danone.

An IFIL statement said its parent company revenues rose 10 percent in comparison with 1995, and it estimated that its consolidated net profit for 1996 will be above the 321 billion lire reported in 1995.
